name: René Jules Dubos
summary: French-educated medical researcher and microbiologist known for discovering antibiotics and developing ecological concepts of infectious disease.

name: Rockefeller Institute for Medical Research
summary: Medical research institute in New York where Dubos conducted much of his career.

name: Harvard School of Public Health
summary: University department where Dubos served as Professor of Comparative Pathology and Tropical Medicine.

name: Marie Louise Bonnet
summary: Dubos's first wife who died of tuberculosis in 1942.

name: Jean Porter Dubos
summary: Dubos's second wife and co-author of The White Plague.

name: Frank Fenner
summary: Australian microbiologist and former laboratory assistant to Dubos.

name: Frank Macfarlane Burnet
summary: Australian medical researcher whose ecological ideas influenced Dubos.

name: Oswald Avery
summary: Biochemist and Dubos's mentor at the Rockefeller Institute.

name: Theobald Smith
summary: American veterinary pathologist whose ideas on host-parasite equilibrium influenced Dubos.

name: Sergei Winogradsky
summary: Russian soil microbiologist whose work inspired Dubos's ecological perspective.

name: Louis Pasteur
summary: French microbiologist whose biography Dubos wrote and whose work he analyzed.

name: Claude Bernard
summary: French physiologist whose concept of milieu interieur influenced Dubos.

name: tyrothricin
summary: Antibacterial substance isolated by Dubos in 1939.

name: BCG vaccine
summary: Vaccine for tuberculosis studied by Dubos and Fenner.

name: The Bacterial Cell
summary: Book by Dubos published in 1945 challenging notions of bacterial fixity.

name: The White Plague
summary: Historical study of tuberculosis co-written by Dubos and his wife.

name: Biochemical Determinants of Microbial Diseases
summary: Book by Dubos published in 1954 outlining his ecological ideas.

name: Trudeau Society
summary: Organization that awarded Dubos the Trudeau Society Medal.

name: Society of American Bacteriologists
summary: Professional organization where Dubos delivered key lectures.

name: New York
summary: City where the Rockefeller Institute and Society of American Bacteriologists were located.

name: Boston
summary: City where Harvard School of Public Health was located.

name: Australia
summary: Country where Frank Fenner conducted myxomatosis studies.
